entries.proposition: Cohort: 46 adults with drug-resistant epilepsy (surgical candidates, mean epilepsy duration about 19-21 years) against 45 healthy outpatient controls matched by age and sex; FSIQ available for only a subset of patients and not for controls.
entries.snippet: FSIQ scores were not assessed in the healthy control group.

entries.proposition: Samples were drawn pre-operatively as part of routine procedures; no timing relative to seizures is controlled and the authors say a single collection is a limitation.
entries.snippet: The DRE blood samples were collected as part of routine preoperative procedures.

entries.proposition: Statistics: Welch t-tests per analyte for two-group comparisons; two-way ANOVA for condition by sex with Sidak post hoc; Pearson correlations; no family-wise correction across the 13 complement and 16 cytokine analytes is described for the t-tests.
entries.snippet: Complement and cytokine comparisons between two groups (DRE and healthy controls) were performed using unpaired t-tests with Welch’s correction (Fig. 1 and Supplementary Fig. 5, Supplementary Table 1).

entries.proposition: Result: serum C1q, C4, C4b, C3, C3b/iC3b, C5, Factor B and Factor H were about 30 percent lower in DRE, with MBL, C2, C3a, C5a and C5b-9 unchanged.
entries.snippet: Compared to healthy individuals, DRE patients showed evidence of lower abundance, by approximately 30%, in the components C1q (p < 0.0001), C4 (p < 0.001), C4b (p < 0.0001), C3 (p = 0.006), C3b/iC3b (p = 0.006), C5 (p = 0.038)
entries.anchor: Results, Abnormal complement cascade components in DRE

entries.snippet: and regulatory Factor B (p < 0.001) and Factor H (p < 0.0001) (Fig. 1C-O).

entries.proposition: Text and abstract present sex-specific complement dysregulation: DRE males lower C3b/iC3b (p = 0.039), DRE females not (p = 0.372).
entries.snippet: However, DRE males had lower levels of C3b/iC3b compared to healthy males (p = 0.039), while DRE females showed no evidence of reduction (p = 0.372).

entries.snippet: However, DRE females showed no evidence of a linear association between levels of MBL and C3b/iC3b (Fig. 3J), suggesting selective disruption of lectin pathway coordination.

entries.snippet: It remains unclear whether the observed decrease in complement levels and altered cytokine/chemokine profiles cause seizures, result from them, or have beneficial or harmful effects in epilepsy.

entries.snippet: Although our literature review did not identify studies linking epilepsy with increased susceptibility to infections or prolonged inflammation, some autoimmune disorders can be comorbid with epilepsy39.
